summary: Frederick James Furnivall (1825–1910) was a linguist who studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He co-founded and taught at the Working Men's College, served as Secretary of the Philological Society, and edited the Oxford English Dictionary.

Frederick M. Asher (1941–2021) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota from circa 1968 to 2021, serving as Professor from circa 1985 until 2021.

Frederick M. Smith works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Ludo Rocher and held positions at the University of Iowa, serving as Professor (attested 2006–2008) and later as Professor Emeritus (attested 2026).

Frederick William Thomas (1867–1956) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Librarian at the India Office Records, taught at UCL and the University of London, and was Boden Professor at Oxford.

Frederik David Kan Bosch (1887–1967) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Jacob Samuel Speyer and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He headed the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies and held professorships at Utrecht and Leiden.

Fredrik Barth (1928–2016) studied at the University of Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen, University of Oslo, and Boston University, and also taught at Emory University and Harvard University.

Friederike Assandri specializes in Sinology and religious studies. She studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer and pursued doctoral studies at Heidelberg University (attested 2002), where she later held an academic post (attested 2013).

Friedhelm Hardy (1943–2004) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Oxford. He served as Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London and Wilde Lecturer at Oxford.

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff (1928–2009) was a Sinologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctorates at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington, Hamburg, and Vienna.

Friedrich August Rosen (1805–1837) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages and later of Sanskrit at University College London and the University of London.

Friedrich August Wolf (1759–1824) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (circa 1777–1779) and held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1783 to 1806.

Friedrich Bechtel (1855–1924) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey and August Fick at Göttingen and Heidelberg. He served as a Dozent at Göttingen and later as Ordinarius for comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg.

Friedrich Benedict Weber (1774–1848) studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1792 to 1795. He held an academic post at European University Viadrina (circa 1799–1811) and served as professor of political economy at the University of Breslau (circa 1814–1848).

Friedrich Bollensen (1809–1896) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, learning Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald. He taught German at Gatchina Orphanage Institute, served as Adjunct Professor at Saint Petersburg, and was Professor of Sanskrit at Kazan.

Friedrich Brockhaus (1838–1895) was an academic who held professorships across several institutions: the University of Jena (circa 1868–1871), the University of Basel (circa 1871–1872), the University of Marburg (circa 1872–1875), and Kiel University (circa 1875–1888).

Friedrich Carl Andreas (1846–1930) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1887–1903) and the University of Göttingen (circa 1903–1930).

Friedrich Christian Diez (1794–1876) was a linguist who studied at the University of Giessen and the University of Göttingen, studying under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker. He held an academic post at the University of Bonn from circa 1823 to 1876.

Friedrich Creuzer (1771–1858) was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Jena and Tübingen, subsequently holding academic posts at the University of Marburg, Heidelberg University, and Leiden University.

Friedrich Delitzsch (1850–1922) was a linguist and historian who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Heinrich Fleischer, Hermann Brockhaus, Georg Curtius, August Dillmann, and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at the universities of Breslau and Berlin.

Friedrich Ernst August Krause (1879–1942) was a Sinologist who studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen from circa 1902 to 1904. He later held an academic post at Heidelberg University from circa 1925 to 1942.
